objectives: Explain why the Most High confounded the language at Babel.
Connect the spirit of Nimrod with the man of sin.
Trace the shortening of lifespans and Abram's beginnings in Ur of the Chaldees.
takeaways: The people being one was not going to produce righteousness, so the Most High confounded their language and scattered them.
There is no doctrine in scripture of all nations as one; the Most High set the bounds of the people by the number of the children of Israel (Deuteronomy 32:7-9).
The man of sin gathers all nations to himself and deifies himself, as Nimrod did in Shinar (2 Thessalonians 2:3-4).
The lifespans fall generation by generation; the word of Genesis 6:3 is taking hold.
Lot was a just man: one that does that which is lawful and right (Ezekiel 18:5).
